genius_advantages.point: Shrinking reported revenue: Q2 2026 revenue $523M (−21% reported; +1% pro forma); restaurant revenue $158M (−23%); FY26 revenue guide −13% to −18% (−2% to −3% pro forma)
Hardware outsourced to Ennoconn (Foxconn subsidiary) from Jan 2026; hardware revenue reported net from Q2 2026

competitor_advantages.point: Huge installed base; restaurant adj. EBITDA margin 36.7% (Q2 2026)
Claims to have "reclaimed the top position in new restaurant deployments" (Dec 2025)

latest_cos_commentary.headline: NCR Voyix, under CEO James G. Kelly since February 2025, claims global #1 POS software installation share and reclaimed the top spot in new restaurant POS deployments as of December 2025.
latest_cos_commentary.genius_exposure: Direct, large-scale competitor to Genius across pos and payments; NCR Voyix (including its Aloha POS line) is one of the largest-scale incumbents in restaurant POS globally, competing head-to-head for enterprise and multi-unit restaurant accounts.
latest_cos_commentary.competitive_timing: Recent leadership change (CEO Kelly, Feb 2025, ex-EVO Payments) and a December 2025 press push emphasizing reclaimed restaurant-deployment leadership suggest an active competitive repositioning effort underway.
latest_cos_commentary.sales_response: Where NCR Voyix/Aloha is the incumbent, expect an operator relationship already built around NCR's platform-led enterprise strategy; probe for specific pain points (support, integration flexibility, cost) rather than assuming displacement is easy given NCR's stated installed-base scale.
latest_cos_commentary.risk_and_uncertainty: Market-leadership and installation figures are NCR Voyix's own claims from its press release, not independently verified third-party data; treat specific numbers (e.g., '#1 globally') as company-reported positioning.

verification_needed: named restaurant customer scope with specific brand names

vendor_claims.value: NCR Voyix currently positions Aloha Next as its restaurant-commerce-platform umbrella.
vendor_claims.limitations_or_conflicts: Product-generation boundaries between Aloha Next and other Aloha families are not explicit.

vendor_claims.value: NCR markets Aloha restaurant POS around order capture/routing and point-of-service payments intended to reduce staff movement and operational friction.
vendor_claims.limitations_or_conflicts: Operational outcome claims were not independently validated.

product_lineage.value: NCR's current pricing estate distinguishes Aloha Cloud from Aloha Essentials, with Essentials described as combining cloud benefits with on-site redundancy.
product_lineage.limitations_or_conflicts: Relationship to Aloha Next and core Aloha POS remains ambiguous.

product_lineage.value: NCR's older Aloha POS documentation site states that it is no longer updated and directs users to a newer DEVEX knowledge hub.
product_lineage.limitations_or_conflicts: Documentation migration does not itself mean the Aloha product is discontinued.

weaknesses.value: A Reddit Aloha discussion contains a third-party technician's report that they could not make a merchant's Aloha payments more reliable.
weaknesses.limitations_or_conflicts: Anonymous single-thread anecdote; hardware, processor and configuration details are unknown.

vulnerabilities.value: Vendor-originated evidence does not prove performance, ROI, reliability, implementation quality, or systemwide deployment; independent validation remains incomplete.
